# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

Resolve the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps between
Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. TP feedback is
scattered across support tickets and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has
been done. This investigation produces the definitive GA scope that all
stability and hardening work is planned against.

## Scope

- Collect and consolidate Tech Preview feedback from support tickets
- Assess the current state of Llama Stack against the GA bar in the four
  dimensions named by the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale
  limits, and error handling
- Produce a gap inventory with severity and GA-bar delta for each gap
- Produce the definitive GA scope document (what is in and out of GA),
  ratified by product and engineering stakeholders

## Acceptance Criteria

- Gap inventory covers API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error
  handling, with each gap rated for severity and impact on the GA bar
- Tech Preview feedback from support tickets is consolidated and reflected in
  the inventory
- A definitive GA scope document is published and ratified by product and
  engineering stakeholders
- The stability and hardening work can be scoped directly from the inventory
  with no remaining unknowns about what GA requires

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and GA bar, producing the definitive GA scope — this epic is the
  primary delivery of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability and upgrade path

## Description

Deliver the GA-bar API stability work for Llama Stack, as concretely specified
by the strategy: a published, versioned API surface carrying a stability
guarantee and deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two
TP releases. This scope is fully specified up front and is not gated by the
GA-readiness assessment; the assessment-driven quality-gap remediation is
tracked as its own gated epic so that this work can proceed immediately.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface; publish an API stability guarantee and a
  deprecation policy
- Implement and test an upgrade path from the last two TP releases

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published APIs are versioned and carry a documented stability guarantee and
  deprecation policy
- Upgrade from each of the last two TP releases is tested and documented

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): published API surface carries a stability guarantee — versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases — delivered by this epic.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

Put the production support posture in place for Llama Stack GA: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. This work is
independent of the GA-readiness assessment — its scope is fully specified by
the strategy — and it reconciles its outputs with the assessment findings
where they intersect (notably scale limits).

Ordering note: the reconciliation acceptance criterion means the supported
configuration matrix cannot be finalized before the GA-readiness assessment
findings (in particular assessed scale limits) are available. This is a
finish-ordering constraint only — the epic's core authoring work (SLO targets,
backport policy, draft matrix) starts immediately and is not blocked by the
assessment.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA distribution
- Define and document the backport policy
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix (deployment shapes,
  provider combinations, and versions that are supported at GA)

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and ratified by product and support stakeholders
- Backport policy is documented
- Supported configuration matrix is published
- Supported configuration matrix is reconciled with the GA-readiness
  assessment findings, in particular assessed scale limits

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): production support posture in place — documented SLO targets,
  backport policy, and supported configuration matrix — delivered by this
  epic.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

Promote TrustyAI safety guardrails from an experimental flag to a supported,
documented integration for GA Llama Stack distributions. The integration
exists today behind an experimental opt-in; this epic makes it a first-class
supported part of the GA distribution, validated against the stabilized,
versioned Llama Stack API surface.

Work-product boundary: this epic is code and validation only. All
user-facing documentation of the integration (configuration, usage, and
support expectations) is authored in the GA documentation uplift owned by
RHOAI Documentation; this epic supplies the technical validation findings
and support-posture decisions that content is reviewed against.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental-flag gating for the TrustyAI guardrails integration
  on GA distributions
- Validate the integration against the stabilized, versioned Llama Stack API
  surface (guardrails run as a Llama Stack safety integration)
- Define the integration's support posture (what is supported, by whom, under
  which SLOs) in coordination with the Llama Stack production support posture
  work owned by the RHOAI GenAI team
- Provide technical validation findings to the RHOAI Documentation team as
  input to the user-facing integration documentation

## Acceptance Criteria

- Guardrails operate on GA Llama Stack distributions without any experimental
  opt-in flag
- The integration is validated against the versioned, stability-guaranteed
  Llama Stack API surface
- The support posture for the integration (what is supported, by whom, under
  which SLOs) is defined and ratified in coordination with the Llama Stack
  production support posture work (SLO targets and support model owned by the
  RHOAI GenAI team), such that the integration's supported scope and SLOs are
  consistent with the GA distribution's support posture

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions — this epic
  delivers the supported integration (flag removal, validation, support
  posture); the user-facing documentation of the integration is delivered by
  the GA documentation uplift epic owned by RHOAI Documentation, which
  depends on this epic's completed validation.

# Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters

## Description

Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate so that the Dashboard enables Llama Stack
management by default for entitled clusters. The management UI already exists
behind a TP opt-in gate; this epic makes it default-on as part of the Llama
Stack GA milestone. The Dashboard change lives in a different repository than
the Llama Stack hardening work and builds against nothing it produces, so this
epic proceeds in parallel with it; the timing constraint — do not expose the
management surface by default before Llama Stack meets the GA quality bar —
is carried by the acceptance criteria below, not by a blocking dependency.

## Scope

- Flip the Llama Stack management feature default to enabled for entitled
  clusters (Dashboard feature flags and defaults are managed via the dashboard
  configuration CR)
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate
- Preserve existing behavior for non-entitled clusters

## Acceptance Criteria

- Entitled clusters see Llama Stack management enabled by default with no
  opt-in required
- Non-entitled clusters are unaffected
- The default-on change ships with the Llama Stack GA milestone — it does not
  expose the management surface by default before Llama Stack meets the GA
  quality bar

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate) — delivered by this epic.

# Llama Stack GA gap remediation

## Description

Remediate the quality gaps inventoried by the GA-readiness assessment (for
example scale limits and error handling) to the GA bar. The size and content
of this work is unknown until the assessment produces the ratified GA scope —
this is the strategy's open question — so the epic is gated on the assessment
outcome and is re-scoped to the assessed gap list. The concretely-specified
API stability and upgrade-path work is tracked separately and is not held
behind this gate.

## Scope

- Remediate the gaps recorded in the ratified GA scope (scale limits, error
  handling, and other inventoried gaps)
- Re-scope the remediation work to the assessed gap list when the GA-readiness
  assessment outcome is available
